key_insight: FERMAT’s representation-based predictors performed better for disease-risk prediction, while generated event sequences performed better for same-day clinical event prediction.
clinical_relevance: Matching the prediction approach to the task may help researchers design more effective tools for disease-risk estimation and clinical event prediction.
method: Trained a 65-million-parameter autoregressive model on longitudinal EHRs from 3.77 million patients.
Compared task-specific predictors using patient representations with predictions derived from generated event sequences.
Evaluated five-year disease risk and same-day diagnosis, prescription, and procedure prediction.
evidence_signal: In testing, representation-based predictors gained 0.098–0.115 in observation-weighted AUROC for three disease risks (n=10,000), while generation achieved 71.0% versus 55.7% Recall@10 for same-day events (n=1,862).
watch_item: Single-hospital data limit generalizability; external validation and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical deployment.
paper_title: FERMAT: An Autoregressive Clinical Foundation Model for Disease Risk and Clinical Event Prediction
